people.name: Thomas Muster
people.extract: Thomas Muster is an Austrian former professional tennis player. He was ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP). Muster won 44 ATP Tour-level singles titles, including the 1995 French Open and eight Masters titles. One of the world's leading clay court players in the 1990s, at his peak he was called "The King of Clay". He is the first Austrian to win a major singles title, followed by Dominic Thiem at the 2020 US Open.
highlights: Won 1995 French Open and eight Masters titles.
First Austrian to win a major singles title.

people.name: Dave Barrett
people.bio: Premier of British Columbia from 1972 to 1975
people.extract: David Barrett was a Canadian politician and social worker in British Columbia. A member of the British Columbia New Democratic Party (BCNDP), he was the 26th premier of British Columbia from 1972 to 1975. He was the first NDP premier in the province.
highlights: Served as 26th premier of British Columbia (1972-1975).
First NDP premier in British Columbia.

people.name: Tom Moody
people.extract: Thomas Masson Moody is a former Australian international cricketer and current Director of Cricket of Sri Lanka Cricket. He ended his long tenure with the Indian Premier League team Sunrisers Hyderabad in August 2022 and was earlier appointed Director of Cricket at Desert Vipers, one of the six franchises in the ILT20, which was scheduled to begin in the UAE in January 2023. Moody was a part of the Australian team that won their first world title during the 1987 Cricket World Cup, and their second in the 1999 Cricket World Cup. He was the coach of the Sri Lankan team which finished as runners-up at the 2007 Cricket World Cup.
highlights: Won 1987 and 1999 Cricket World Cups with Australia.
Coached Sri Lanka to 2007 Cricket World Cup runners-up.
Current Director of Cricket of Sri Lanka Cricket.
